projects.title: CUSA Crimson Raiders Discord Bot
projects.meta: Discord Bot developed in Python for CUSA
projects.desc: This background check bot system was one of many I did for this bot, mostly to automate a bunch of HICOM duties. It works essentially by going into an empty Roblox alt account via that account's token, and searching up the user inputted. It checks things like Account Age, Friend count, Badge count, Group count, and then goes through all of the user's friends - parsing their names to find any names similar to the original account name to see if they can be flagged as alt accounts. For example, if robloxuser was friends with robloxuser_alt, the bot would detect that and flag it as a suspicious alternative account. The bot will allow for a count of one maximum red flag before failing the user's background check - and logging it in a private channel for HICOM to see.

projects.title: coldd Development Marketplace Bot
projects.meta: Discord Bot developed in Python for coldd
projects.note: Based off of HiddenDevs' marketplace bot
projects.desc: This was a very extensive system I did for a company I co-ran, "coldd Development". It spanned about 3k+ lines of code in Visual Studio Code prior to its optimization, created in mid-2024. It was essentially a remake of HiddenDev's (.gg/hd) old marketplace posting system bot. It entailed some simple devex commands (/devex-robux, /devex-currency), etc. The main premise of the bot was the very extensive marketplace system, which had three options: "Hiring", "For-Hire", and "Tutorial". Tutorial walked the user through how to use the system, although, I will admit it was improved later. Hiring and For-Hire began the post preview system, [Fig.1] which helped the user customise their post before sending it to mods for approval. The customization system included things like a description, title, a contact method, a payment type, a role (Scripter, Builder, etc) and images. After the user was satisfied with their creation, they'd submit it for review with an ID - and moderators would either deny or approve it with a custom embed [Fig.2]. All in all, for slightly earlier in my discord bot coding existence, it was the hardest bot I've ever made and pushed me far out of my comfort zone (my skills are vastly different compared to 2024).

projects.title: LuaShield Obfuscator
projects.desc: This was a several-month long side project I always had in mind - I thought it would be way easier than it was, but there are many issues that pop up with obfuscation. First off, how? How do you obfuscate it? Do you make it harder to read, or impossible to read? I had seen from some friends in the development community a paid service which offered impossible to read obfuscation, which could condense several thousand-line long scripts into one line (albeit LOADS of characters). The easier (much easier) route was obviously to make it hard to read, but I decided to take the hard route like always. It had me set up many things that I'm not going to mention here (may patent in the future 😉) and ended up being several tens of thousands of lines long of code (quite repetitive). It will be available for the public to use soon, along with its free counterpart, a deobfuscator. In its current state I haven't released the more complex obfuscation method, but it will be released when finished.

projects.title: coldd.dev Website
projects.desc: I built this site alongside a team of 3 other developers, taking us months. It has a custom ordering system which accepts card, crypto, paypal and robux - it has a full sign in and account creation system with emails that are sent to the user, along with other related features such as password and account recovery. It has a full blog posting area as well as a custom gifting system. It has a complex referral system (where you get paid for referring other friends to buy products), a fully custom robux purchasing system where when you place an order a bot will create a gamepass with the price in under 10 seconds and give you the gamepass to order with, and once purchased it will check your username for eligibility. The site also comes with a custom USD/Robux switcher in the top left along with a cart viewer, although the currency can be switched from any UN-recognized currency rather than just being USD (e.g., AUD, GBP, EUR, JPY). It has a custom product searching page where the user can filter via things like price, category, free products, on-sale products, recommended products, and many more. It also comes with an account creation and management system, where you can manage things in your personal dashboard such as your current licenses, your wishlist and referrals, your purchase history, account settings, and more! You can currently link your account to Google, Roblox & Discord - although we are looking into more ways soon. The site has a custom notification system, where you get notified whenever there is an ongoing sale or you are eligible for a free product, or after you buy a product. Along the sidebar, there is a cart with an automatic discount depending on how much you've spent. Back on checkout, there are also discounts available for staff and other important members you can apply via discount codes. There is a fully custom review system, an email marketing system, a bundle and weekly deal system, an FAQ page, and a lot more legal pages for our legal team. There is also an admin panel I could go on about for ages (you can see a little sneak peek in the "Statistics Page" image), but can't share too much of that (including a massive product upload system, more complex than it sounds).
